answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of fresh computational work per agent, setting a fixed price that prevents cheap identity flooding. The verifier acts as a beacon, guiding incoming proofs toward a prism of analysis that confirms each task is non-replayable. While an honest agent pays this base cost, an attacker managing 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units, hitting a wharf of exhaustion. Any duplicate submission triggers an identity burn.
